dockerfile.scenario: A simple single-stage Dockerfile has a material instruction question
dockerfile.expected: Trigger the profile and establish syntax, platform, stage, and project policy

dockerfile.scenario: An ordinary application change has no Dockerfile concern
dockerfile.expected: Non-trigger

dockerfile.scenario: The task changes only Docker Compose behavior
dockerfile.expected: Non-trigger; route to the Compose or project owner

dockerfile.scenario: A syntax directive is unsupported or its frontend identity is unknown
dockerfile.expected: Red until the selected frontend and feature support are established

dockerfile.scenario: A parser directive appears after an ordinary comment, empty line, or instruction
dockerfile.expected: Orange because the intended directive is ineffective; Red when consequential behavior depends on the false directive claim

dockerfile.scenario: Linux versus Windows container semantics are unclear
dockerfile.expected: Orange pending exact platform, escape, path, shell, and instruction evidence; unsupported claims are Red

dockerfile.scenario: A base image uses a mutable tag
dockerfile.expected: Yellow or Orange under project ownership; absent authority or verification at a consequential boundary is Red

dockerfile.scenario: A digest-pinned base is required by project policy
dockerfile.expected: Green or Yellow under project policy after platform, update, provenance, and rollback boundaries are verified

dockerfile.scenario: A global ARG before FROM is assumed to be in ordinary stage scope
dockerfile.expected: Yellow; map global and stage scope and re-declare the ARG in a stage before ordinary stage use

dockerfile.scenario: A named multi-stage build has coherent build and runtime stages
dockerfile.expected: Green when names and dependencies make the stage graph, target, and copies unambiguous

dockerfile.scenario: COPY --from names the wrong, missing, or ambiguous stage or source
dockerfile.expected: Red until the artifact source and destination stage are unambiguous

dockerfile.scenario: The Dockerfile has unnecessary stage proliferation
dockerfile.expected: At least Yellow; apply stage-count, responsibility, and coupling rules before escalation

dockerfile.scenario: The target stage is selected by project policy
dockerfile.expected: Green or Yellow after verifying the project-owned target graph without choosing it

dockerfile.scenario: Automatic build and target platform arguments control a stage
dockerfile.expected: Orange while mapping BUILD and TARGET scope, native versus cross execution, and toolchain support; unsupported claims are Red

dockerfile.scenario: A shell-form RUN relies on expansion, pipelines, or shell failure behavior
dockerfile.expected: Yellow when expansion is deliberate and trusted; pair a shell profile only when its semantics are independently material

dockerfile.scenario: An exec-form instruction supplies a fixed argument vector
dockerfile.expected: Green for a fixed supported argument vector; do not assume shell expansion or shell builtins

dockerfile.scenario: An untrusted value reaches shell interpretation
dockerfile.expected: Red source-to-shell stop

dockerfile.scenario: ARG or ENV carries a protected value
dockerfile.expected: Red because the value can reach image configuration, history, cache, provenance, output, or later layers

dockerfile.scenario: A package-index update is separated unsafely from installation
dockerfile.expected: Orange when the selected package manager requires one owned update and installation transaction; do not universalize the rule

dockerfile.scenario: One RUN command chain obscures failure ownership
dockerfile.expected: Apply the maximum RUN-command band; normally Orange once failure ownership is obscured

dockerfile.scenario: SHELL changes the meaning of later shell-form instructions
dockerfile.expected: Orange while mapping later shell-form instructions; unsafe or falsely supported behavior is Red

dockerfile.scenario: .dockerignore excludes a file that a later instruction requires
dockerfile.expected: Orange until context and ignore ownership are reconciled; source review cannot claim a successful copy or build

dockerfile.scenario: The build context contains unintended protected or large files
dockerfile.expected: Protected exposure is Red; excessive unrelated context is a structural and cache warning

dockerfile.scenario: COPY fully expresses the required local or stage-owned transfer
dockerfile.expected: Prefer the narrower semantics without turning the preference into an automatic rewrite

dockerfile.scenario: ADD introduces a remote URL, Git source, or automatic archive extraction
dockerfile.expected: Remote ADD without authority, immutability, and verification is Red; deliberate local extraction is Yellow or Orange with bounded evidence

dockerfile.scenario: File ownership, mode, user, or permission effects are material
dockerfile.expected: Normally Orange while establishing stage, platform, source metadata, runtime user, and rollback; unresolved consequential access is Red

dockerfile.scenario: A multi-stage artifact copy deliberately narrows final image contents
dockerfile.expected: Green or Yellow for an exact named-stage artifact set; do not infer build success or absence of unrelated metadata

dockerfile.scenario: The Dockerfile is generated or vendor-owned
dockerfile.expected: Classify and change the authorized owner or generator; semantic Red stops still control

dockerfile.scenario: The final runtime configuration remains root without project rationale
dockerfile.expected: Red when the consequential user, ownership, or permission boundary is unresolved

dockerfile.scenario: ENTRYPOINT and CMD interaction or override behavior is misunderstood
dockerfile.expected: Orange until the exact form and override matrix is established; unsafe runtime behavior is Red

dockerfile.scenario: A health-check command can false-pass or expose protected output
dockerfile.expected: Red until status, timing, timeout, output, and protected-data behavior are safe

dockerfile.scenario: Signal handling or STOPSIGNAL behavior is material
dockerfile.expected: Orange while establishing the runtime process and platform contract; unsafe or unsupported behavior is Red

dockerfile.scenario: ONBUILD creates hidden downstream build behavior
dockerfile.expected: At least Orange; unresolved downstream context, source, or mutation ownership is Red

dockerfile.scenario: VOLUME creates persistence, initialization, or mutation ambiguity
dockerfile.expected: Orange until image metadata, runtime ownership, initialization, persistence, mutation, and rollback are explicit; consequential ambiguity is Red

dockerfile.scenario: A BuildKit secret mount is declared for a project-approved protected input
dockerfile.expected: Green or Yellow after syntax, identity, command use, output, cache, and provenance boundaries are verified; the mount alone is not proof

dockerfile.scenario: A protected value is copied, printed, persisted, or exported into a layer or build output
dockerfile.expected: Red protected-data stop

dockerfile.scenario: A cache or bind mount changes reproducibility or shared mutation
dockerfile.expected: Orange while establishing contents, sharing, ownership, invalidation, cleanup, and clean-build fallback

dockerfile.scenario: Repository policy is stricter than the profile fallback
dockerfile.expected: Stricter repository policy controls

dockerfile.scenario: A destructive or networked build action lacks authority
dockerfile.expected: Red authority stop

dockerfile.scenario: A maintained Dockerfile crosses a warning or crisis threshold
dockerfile.expected: Apply classification, coupling, decomposition, bounded-exception, and rollback rules
